# Behavioral Specification: AON Timer Core

## Overview

The AON timer core provides two independent 32-bit up-counting timers:

- A **wakeup timer**, which can be prescaled and generates a wakeup interrupt when it reaches a programmed threshold.
- A **watchdog timer**, which generates an interrupt at a first threshold (bark) and a reset request at a second threshold (bite).

The module exposes the current values of its programmable control, threshold, and count registers. It also accepts register writes that update those values.

## Reset Behavior

When reset is asserted:

- All timers must be cleared to zero.
- All timer enables must be cleared.
- The wakeup prescaler must be cleared.
- The watchdog pause control must be cleared.
- All threshold values must be cleared.
- The wakeup interrupt output, watchdog interrupt output, and watchdog reset request output must be deasserted.

All state updates occur synchronously with the always-on clock.

## Programmable State

The module has the following software-visible state:

- Wakeup timer enable.
- Wakeup prescaler value.
- Wakeup threshold value.
- Wakeup count value.
- Watchdog timer enable.
- Watchdog pause-in-sleep control.
- Watchdog bark threshold value.
- Watchdog bite threshold value.
- Watchdog count value.

Writes to control registers, threshold registers, and count registers must take effect on the next active clock edge. The current values of all programmable state must be available on the module’s read outputs.

If a count register is written at the same time as a normal count increment would occur, the written value must take precedence. The count outputs reflect the new written value after the update.

## Enable Qualifiers

The module receives independent enable qualifiers:

- One qualifier gates the wakeup prescaler.
- One qualifier gates the wakeup count.
- One qualifier gates the watchdog count.

A qualifier must be in the “On” state for the associated counter to advance. If a qualifier is not “On”, the associated counter must hold its current value. Disabling a timer must not clear its count; the count resumes from its current value when re-enabled.

## Wakeup Timer Behavior

The wakeup timer consists of a 12-bit prescaler and a 32-bit up counter.

The wakeup prescaler runs only when the wakeup timer is enabled and its associated enable qualifier is “On”.

The wakeup count increments by one each time the prescaler period elapses. If the programmed prescaler value is N, the wakeup count must advance once every N+1 always-on clock cycles. A prescaler value of zero must cause the count to advance every clock cycle.

The wakeup count must hold its value when:

- The wakeup timer is disabled.
- The wakeup count enable qualifier is not “On”.
- The prescaler period has not elapsed.

The wakeup count must also be writable by software. Writing a value to the wakeup count loads the counter with that value, regardless of whether the timer is enabled.

The wakeup interrupt output must be asserted when a wakeup count increment occurs and the current count value equals the wakeup threshold value. The output is asserted in the clock cycle of that qualifying increment. The count is not held at the threshold; it continues incrementing normally.

## Watchdog Timer Behavior

The watchdog timer is a 32-bit up counter with no prescaler.

The watchdog count increments by one every always-on clock cycle when:

- The watchdog timer is enabled.
- The watchdog count enable qualifier is “On”.
- The watchdog is not paused.

The watchdog count must hold its value when:

- The watchdog timer is disabled.
- The watchdog count enable qualifier is not “On”.
- The pause-in-sleep control is set and the module is in sleep mode.

Writing to the watchdog count loads the counter with the written value. Writing zero clears the watchdog count and thereby “pets” the watchdog.

The watchdog interrupt output must be asserted when a watchdog count increment occurs and the current count equals the watchdog bark threshold value.

The watchdog reset request output must be asserted when a watchdog count increment occurs and the current count equals the watchdog bite threshold value.

The bark interrupt and bite reset request are independent. If both thresholds are equal, both outputs must be asserted on the same qualifying increment.

Asserting the bite reset request must not by itself clear or reload the watchdog count. The watchdog count continues to operate unless it is written by software or reset by the system.

## Sleep Mode and Watchdog Pause

The sleep mode indication is an input to the module.

- If the watchdog pause-in-sleep control is cleared, sleep mode must not stop the watchdog timer.
- If the watchdog pause-in-sleep control is set, the watchdog count must stop advancing while sleep mode is active.
- When sleep mode exits or the pause control is cleared, the watchdog count must resume advancing.

The wakeup timer must not be affected by sleep mode.

## Event Outputs

The interrupt and reset request outputs are pulse-style events: they are asserted for the clock cycle in which the qualifying timer increment occurs. They are not held until software acknowledges them.

The event outputs must only be generated when the associated count is actively incrementing. Simply writing a count value equal to a threshold must not, by itself, assert an interrupt or reset request.

## Counter Wrap Behavior

The timers are 32-bit up counters. When a counter is at its maximum value and another increment occurs, it must wrap to zero. Threshold comparisons are evaluated before the wrap, so a threshold equal to the maximum value generates its event on the same increment that causes the wrap.
